pageCache.pageTitle: Our Church Partnership - Rowde C of E Primary Academy
pageCache.text:
Our Church Partnership
With God's guidance, sowing the seeds of success, nurturing and inspiring pupils and adults to flourish.
Rowde Primary Academy and St Matthew's Church have a long and valued partnership, reflecting the school's place at the heart of our village community. As a Church of England school, our Christian vision and values shape school life, and we are proud to work closely with the church to enrich the experiences of our children and strengthen our links with the wider community.
Throughout the year, we gather together in St Matthew's Church to celebrate key moments in the Christian calendar, including Harvest, Christmas, Easter and our Year 6 Leavers' Service. These occasions provide opportunities for reflection, celebration and worship as a whole school community. At the Leavers' Service, every Year 6 pupil is presented with a special book from the church as they prepare for the next stage of their journey.
We are grateful for the many members of the church community who regularly support school life. The Open the Book team visit twice each month to bring Bible stories to life through interactive storytelling, often involving the children in the performances. In addition, Reverend Norma Fergusson and Richard Fergusson visit every other week to lead Collective Worship, helping children explore how our worship themes connect with the Bible and Jesus' teachings in ways that are meaningful and relevant to their everyday lives.
Our partnership extends beyond worship. We regularly use St Matthew's Church to enrich the teaching of Christianity within Religious Education and to provide children with opportunities to experience the church as a place of worship, reflection and community. We also enjoy supporting and celebrating events within the church and wider village, sharing these opportunities with families through our newsletters and communications.
We are delighted that Frances Hall, a member of St Matthew's congregation, serves on our Academy Council. Frances plays an important role in strengthening the partnership between school and church, providing support, challenge and encouragement as we continue to develop as a flourishing Church of England school.
Our Christian vision, Learn • Grow • Love, inspired by Jesus' Parable of the Mustard Seed (Matthew 13:31–32), continues to guide everything we do. Alongside our six Christian values of Respect, Optimism, Wisdom, Determination, Enthusiasm and Love, our partnership with St Matthew's Church helps our children develop spiritually, serve their community and understand how faith can inspire people to make a positive difference in the world.

pageCache.pageTitle: Vision and Values - Rowde C of E Primary Academy
pageCache.text:
Vision and Values
Our Vision
Our Mission
To create a loving, kind environment where every child is empowered to achieve success and flourish.
Our Christian Values
Respect • Optimism • Wisdom • Determination • Enthusiasm • Love
At Rowde C of E Primary Academy, everything we do is centred around our vision to Learn, Grow and Love. We believe every child, every member of staff and every family is part of our school community and we are committed to nurturing, supporting and inspiring everyone to flourish.
Our Christian vision is rooted in Jesus' Parable of the Mustard Seed (Matthew 13:31–32). Although the mustard seed is one of the smallest seeds, when it is nurtured it grows into a strong tree that provides shelter for others. This reminds us that every child has unique gifts and enormous potential. With love, encouragement, challenge and God's guidance, every child can grow in confidence, wisdom and character, developing the knowledge and skills they need to flourish both now and in the future.
Just as the mustard tree grows strong enough for birds to rest safely among its branches, we strive to create a school where everyone feels welcomed, valued and loved. We believe that every child can succeed, regardless of their starting point, and that every individual has an important contribution to make to our school community and the wider world.
Our vision shapes every aspect of school life. We are committed to developing happy, confident young people with enquiring minds, a love of learning and a deep respect for themselves, for others and for God's world. Through a broad and ambitious curriculum, high expectations and a culture of belonging, we help our children develop the resilience, compassion and adaptability they need to thrive in secondary school and beyond.
Our six Christian values bring our vision to life each day. They are explicitly taught, modelled by adults and woven throughout our curriculum, collective worship and daily interactions. To help even our youngest children understand what these values look like in action, each is connected to a Bible story that we return to throughout the year.
Together, our vision, mission and values create a school where children are inspired to learn with curiosity, grow with confidence and love with compassion. They guide every decision we make and every relationship we build, ensuring that Rowde is a place where everyone can flourish.
You can read more about each of our Christian values and the Bible passages that inspire them below.
Rowde Values and Explanations
Respect – The Good Samaritan (Luke 10:25–37)
Determination – The Paralysed Man (Mark 2:1–12)

British Values and Equalities
At Rowde C of E Primary Academy, we believe that preparing children for life in modern Britain is about much more than learning facts. It is about developing kind, thoughtful and responsible citizens who understand how to contribute positively to their communities and the wider world.
Our Christian vision of Learn • Grow • Love underpins everything we do. Through our curriculum, collective worship, relationships and daily school life, children develop the knowledge, skills and character needed to become active citizens who value themselves, others and the world around them.
British Values at Rowde
The Department for Education requires schools to actively promote the fundamental British Values. At Rowde, these are not taught as a standalone subject but are woven throughout every aspect of school life and form an important part of our Personal Development curriculum.
We teach and promote:
These values are lived every day through our behaviour curriculum, We Are Rowde expectations, pupil leadership opportunities, democratic voting, curriculum learning, collective worship and the relationships we build across our school community.
Children revisit each value throughout their time at Rowde, developing from understanding themselves and those around them to becoming active citizens who are ready to make a positive contribution to society.
You can view our British Values progression below:
British Values at Rowde AY26-27
Equality, Diversity and Inclusion
We believe that every child is uniquely created, valued and loved. Our aim is to ensure that every member of our school community feels welcomed, respected and able to flourish.
Children are taught that:
Through our curriculum, collective worship and everyday interactions, children learn about equality, diversity and the importance of respecting those whose experiences, beliefs or backgrounds may be different from their own.
As part of this learning, children develop an age-appropriate understanding of the protected characteristics identified within the Equality Act 2010. These are thoughtfully woven throughout our curriculum and Personal Development programme, helping children to understand fairness, inclusion and the importance of treating everyone with kindness and respect.
The protected characteristics are:
You can find out more in the documents below: Protected Characteristics at Rowde
Equality Information and Objectives Policy
One way we bring these values to life is through our Jigsaw PSHE programme and weekly Picture News sessions. These provide children with regular opportunities to discuss current events, explore different viewpoints and develop the knowledge, skills and understanding needed to become kind, thoughtful and active citizens. You can find out more about these resources below:

At Rowde, we are a very special school community with one clear vision: to inspire everyone to Learn, Grow and Love. We believe every child and every member of our community has unique gifts and talents and we are committed to nurturing, supporting and inspiring everyone to flourish.
It is a privilege to be Headteacher of Rowde, having previously served as both a Key Stage 2 teacher and Deputy Headteacher. Together with our dedicated staff, supportive families, governors, Acorn Education Trust and colleagues across the Diocese, we continue to build a school where children thrive academically, socially, emotionally and spiritually.
When you join Rowde, you become part of a family rooted in love, kindness and belonging. Our Christian values of Respect, Optimism, Wisdom, Determination, Enthusiasm and Love shape everything we do, guiding our relationships, our learning and our decisions each day. We have high expectations for both behaviour and achievement because we believe every child deserves the opportunity to succeed and to discover all they are capable of.
Our aim is not simply to prepare children for their next stage of education, but to equip them with the confidence, character, knowledge and values that will enable them to flourish throughout their lives. We are passionate about creating an environment where children feel safe, valued and challenged, knowing that strong relationships and emotional wellbeing provide the foundations for exceptional learning.
We know that children achieve their very best when school and home work together in partnership. I hope our website gives you a flavour of what makes Rowde such a special place but nothing compares to experiencing it for yourself. I would be delighted to welcome you to our school, show you around our wonderful learning environment and introduce you to our fantastic children and dedicated staff.
We are incredibly proud of our Rowde family and look forward to welcoming yours.

pageCache.pageTitle: Collective Worship - Rowde C of E Primary Academy
pageCache.text:
Collective Worship
Intent
At Rowde, Collective Worship is the heartbeat of our school. Every morning we come together as one community to pause, reflect, celebrate and grow. We believe children flourish when they feel they belong, so worship provides a shared space where everyone is welcomed, valued and encouraged to explore life's big questions together. It is one of the most special parts of our day and helps us live out our vision to Learn • Grow • Love.
Rooted in our Christian vision, worship helps us explore the teachings of Jesus, deepen our understanding of our Christian values and develop spiritually. Inspired by Jesus' Parable of the Mustard Seed (Matthew 13:31–32), our worship encourages every child to flourish. Through stories from the Bible, current events, inspiring books and opportunities for prayer and reflection, children are encouraged to ask life's big questions, appreciate different perspectives and consider how they can make a positive difference in the world around them.
As a Church of England school, our worship is distinctly Christian whilst remaining welcoming, inclusive and accessible to everyone, regardless of faith or background.
Through Collective Worship we aim to:
Implementation
We gather together every morning to begin the day as a school community. Worship is carefully planned across the year to reflect the Christian calendar, our Personal Development curriculum and events happening within the wider world. Using resources such as Picture News, Roots and Fruits and high-quality children's literature, we help children make meaningful connections between faith, values and everyday life.
Each act of worship follows four simple stages:
Our worship is enriched through music, singing, artwork, stories, photography, guided reflections and opportunities for children to participate and lead.
Our weekly pattern
Monday The Headteacher introduces the weekly theme through Picture News, current events or one of our Christian values.
Tuesday We continue to explore the week's theme, making connections to our Christian values, life at Rowde and the wider world. Through discussion and reflection, children consider how they can live out the week's learning in their everyday actions.
Wednesday Understanding the Bible – We explore the weekly theme through connected Bible stories and the teachings of Jesus. On alternate weeks, this worship is led by our valued Open the Book team or Reverend Norma and Richard Fergusson, helping children discover how God's message continues to guide and inspire our lives today.
Thursday Reading Worship – We enjoy a carefully chosen picture book linked to the week's theme, developing both our Christian values and our love of reading.
Friday Celebration Worship – Together we celebrate our Value Champions, birthdays and achievements both in and beyond school. This is one of our favourite worships of the week as we celebrate the achievements, kindness and character of our children, both in and beyond school. Parents are warmly invited to join us every Friday morning at 8.50am.
Throughout the year, we also gather at St Matthew's Church to celebrate Harvest, Christmas, Easter and our Year 6 Leavers' Service, strengthening our partnership with the church and wider village community.
Visitors regularly enrich our worship, and families are kept informed about our weekly themes through the Headteacher's newsletter.
Impact
Collective Worship plays a central role in enabling our children to flourish. Through worship, pupils develop a deeper understanding of our Christian vision and values, grow in confidence to reflect on life's big questions and recognise how the teachings of Jesus can inspire everyday choices.
Children become increasingly thoughtful, compassionate and respectful, developing a strong sense of belonging within our school community while learning to value the beliefs and experiences of others. Worship nurtures spirituality, celebrates diversity and encourages children to make a positive difference through their words and actions.
The quality and impact of Collective Worship are continually reviewed through pupil voice, staff and Academy Council feedback, observations and ongoing evaluation. As part of Acorn Education Trust's Church School Flourishing Programme, we work closely with colleagues across the Trust and Salisbury Diocese to continually develop and strengthen our worship, ensuring it remains engaging, authentic and rooted in our Christian vision.
We hope every child leaves Rowde with joyful memories of worship, a growing understanding of God's love, confidence to ask life's big questions and the inspiration to live out our vision to Learn • Grow • Love wherever life takes them.

pageCache.pageTitle: Vision and Values - Rowde C of E Primary Academy
pageCache.text:
Vision and Values
Learn - Grow - Love
One community Learning and growing together Sharing the love of God
At Rowde, our vision is to develop happy young people with enquiring minds, a spirit of curiosity, love and respect for themselves, others and the environment so that they will have the skills, resilience and adaptability to thrive in a rapidly changing world.
Our Rowde school's Christian ethos, 'Learn-Grow-Love', is underpinned by Jesus’ mustard seed parable: from the smallest seeds grow the greatest shrubs (Mt13v31-32). Valuing our community, together, we embody our vision: “With God’s guidance; sowing the seeds of success; nurturing and inspiring pupils and adults to flourish."
Just like the mustard tree flourishes and grows to hold a valuable position in the garden, we want to see every pupil flourish in their learning, their relationships with others and their personal growth. We aim to give our pupils the best start, preparing them for their secondary education and their role in modern British society.
While the mustard seed is tiny, with soil, water, air and sunlight it grows, becomes strong and attracts the birds to rest among its branches. We believe that all of our pupils have the potential to do well, to succeed in their learning and to become a valued member of society, regardless of their starting point. At Rowde C of E Primary Academy, every member of our school community is valued and cherished; both as an individual and for the contribution they make to the school body.
Acorn Education Trust Vision and Values
As a valued part of the Acorn Education Trust, we are supported by the Senior Executive team to develop our own strong, individual Christian vision, values and identity. We receive termly visits, attend meetings and have frequent training on improving and developing ourselves as a Church School. The vision and values of the Trust itself is focused on one core mission: 'Preparing young people for their world in their time.' Acorn Education Trust ensure that every Acorn school thrives, ensuring the foundations of excellence, which you can see below, are evident in all that they do. These foundations are the roots of the Trust and align well with our Rowde values. Both at Rowde and the Trust, we recognise the importance active and visual leadership, opportunities for all and putting the needs of our staff, pupils and community first.
You can read more about Acorn Education Trust's Vision and Values here:

pageCache.pageTitle: Our Christian Values - Rowde C of E Primary Academy
pageCache.text:
Our Christian Values
From the smallest seeds grow the greatest shrubs
MATTHEW 13:32
Through our Christian ethos, our core values are: Respect, Optimism, Wisdom, Determination, Enthusiasm and Love. These values are built into the ethos and teaching of the school and are modelled by everyone who works at Rowde C of E Primary Academy. We also teach the children about the importance of British values, including democracy, rule of law and individual liberty.
Our vision and values underpin everything we do at Rowde and are an integral part of all policies and procedures in the school. They are discussed and referenced in every act of Collective Worship when we come together in the mornings. We display the values in all of our classrooms using images and quotes from the Bible and elsewhere, to help the children fully understand what they mean and how they link to their own lives. To develop this further, each value is linked to a simple story from the Bible which enables children to deepen their understanding. We are in the process of teaching the children these stories (as shown below), with their key messages, and we make connections to these and our values on a daily basis.
Over the year, each class builds a floor book with their reflections and responses to collective worship and our values, illustrating how these have been developed through different aspects of class life.
Our values are also the foundations of our behaviour policy, and we use them to talk to the children about their actions, to help them understand consequences. This supports the children in making changes and choices to ensure they are following our values within school and in their own lives at home. Everyone understands that “We are Rowde”.
We celebrate our values in our Friday celebration Collective Worship. One child from each class is nominated every week, by either the teacher or their peers, to be value champion!
You can read more about the values and the connected passages from the Bible, below.
Rowde Values and Explanations
Respect: The Good Samaritan (Luke 10:25-37)
Optimism: Jesus heals Jairus’ daughter (Mark 5:21-43)
Determination: A paralysed man (Mark 2:1-12)

pageCache.text:
Wraparound care - Rascals
At Rowde C of E Primary Academy, we understand that family life can be busy. That's why we offer Rascals, our friendly and flexible wraparound care, providing a safe, nurturing and enjoyable environment before and after the school day.
Whether your child enjoys getting creative, playing outdoors, relaxing with friends or taking part in one of our exciting activities, Rascals offers something for everyone. Our caring staff (who the children know well) ensure that children feel happy, secure and well looked after, allowing them to begin and end each day in a calm, positive environment.
Before School Care
Children can enjoy a healthy breakfast before school, including: cereal, toast and pastries, fresh fruit, yoghurt, fruit juice
Breakfast Club provides a relaxed start to the day, helping children arrive in class ready to learn.
After School Care
Children can choose how they spend their time after school, whether that's unwinding with quieter activities or joining one of our organised clubs.
Activities regularly include: arts and crafts, LEGO, football, dance, books and biscuits, board games and outdoor play.
A healthy snack is provided for all children, with an additional snack served during the later session.
Why Choose Us?
Rascals is more than childcare—it's an extension of our school family, where children continue to learn, grow and love beyond the classroom!
Safe and welcoming environment
Caring, experienced staff
Flexible sessions to suit busy families
Healthy breakfast and snacks included
Exciting activities refreshed each term
How to Register
Booking is open now via ParentMail. If you would like to find out more about Rascals or have any questions, please contact the school office. We'd be delighted to help.

Special Educational Needs and Disabilities (SEND)
All children are different and learn at different rates; all have their own individual needs. At Rowde, we cater for all our children's learning needs and abilities through adjustment, support, differentiation and appropriate challenge.
As a school, we are continually monitoring our Special Needs provision recognising that children need support in a variety of ways, at different times in their school life and for different periods of time. We are committed to providing early intervention and providing the best possible support for our children. We value the role that parents play in their children’s education and staff are always available if you have any concerns.
The Primary aim is to integrate pupils with Special Educational Needs into the academic and social life of the school and to enable pupils to work to their full potential.
The school’s SEND co-ordinator (SENDCo) is Miss Lucy Adams who can be contacted via:
lucy.adams@rowde.wilts.sch.uk

pageCache.pageTitle: SATs results and performance - Rowde C of E Primary Academy
pageCache.text:
SATs results and performance
School and College Performance Tables are produced by the Department for Education (DfE) and published online. They provide information about pupil attainment and progress at the end of Key Stage 2 and enable comparisons with other schools locally and nationally. They also include information about areas such as school finances and staffing.
Alongside published performance information, we carefully track the progress and attainment of every pupil throughout their time at Rowde. Regular assessment enables teachers and leaders to identify strengths, respond to gaps in learning and ensure that children receive the support and challenge they need to flourish.
As a small school, our published data should always be considered in the context of individual cohorts. With relatively small numbers of pupils in each year group, the performance of one child can represent a significant percentage of the overall results. Cohorts also vary from year to year, including in the proportion of pupils with additional or special educational needs.
For this reason, we look closely at the progress and achievement of individual children as well as headline percentages. Our focus is on ensuring that every child makes strong progress from their individual starting points, is appropriately challenged and is supported to achieve their potential.

pageCache.pageTitle: Modern Foreign Languages - Rowde C of E Primary Academy
pageCache.text:
Modern Foreign Languages
Intent
At Rowde Primary Academy, we believe that learning a foreign language opens the door to new cultures, perspectives and opportunities. Through our ambitious and engaging French curriculum, children develop the confidence, knowledge and skills needed to communicate in another language while fostering curiosity about the wider world.
From Year 3 to Year 6, pupils progressively develop their listening, speaking, reading and writing skills alongside their understanding of French phonics, vocabulary and grammar. We encourage children to become confident communicators who are willing to take risks, recognising that making mistakes is an important part of learning.
Learning French also develops children's understanding of different cultures and traditions, helping them to recognise similarities, celebrate differences and develop respect for others. Alongside our French curriculum, we celebrate a Language of the Term through collective worship and wider school life, introducing children to a range of world languages and cultures and further enriching their cultural capital.
By the end of Key Stage 2, we aim for every child to have developed a lifelong interest in languages and the confidence to continue language learning beyond primary school.
Implementation
French is taught weekly from Year 3 to Year 6 using the Language Angels Scheme of Work, which provides a carefully sequenced curriculum aligned to the National Curriculum.
Children progressively acquire and apply an increasingly sophisticated bank of vocabulary, phonics, grammatical knowledge and language structures through engaging, age-appropriate topics. Learning is carefully sequenced so that previously taught vocabulary and grammar are revisited regularly through retrieval activities, enabling children to strengthen their long-term memory and build confidence over time.
Lessons provide regular opportunities for children to:
Grammar is taught explicitly through a carefully planned progression, enabling children to understand how language works and apply this knowledge independently. French learning is enriched through songs, stories, festivals, traditions, geography, food and comparisons between life in France and the UK, helping children understand language within authentic cultural contexts.
Teachers use ongoing formative assessment alongside end-of-unit assessments to identify misconceptions, celebrate progress and inform future teaching.
listen to authentic spoken French;
develop accurate pronunciation and intonation;
read increasingly challenging texts;
Impact
By the time children leave Rowde Primary Academy, they have developed the confidence and skills to communicate in basic French through speaking, listening, reading and writing.
Children leave us able to:
Beyond language skills, pupils develop resilience, confidence and a curiosity about the wider world. They gain an appreciation of different cultures and traditions, understand the value of learning languages and are well prepared for continued language study at secondary school.

pageCache.pageTitle: Physical Education (PE) - Rowde C of E Primary Academy
pageCache.text:
Physical Education (PE)
Intent
At Rowde we believe that PE is a vital part of educating the whole child, ensuring that they have the skills, knowledge and understanding to lead a healthy life now and in the future. We believe that PE provides children with the opportunity to learn about physiology, health, well-being, relationships and personal target setting and challenges. This could be within competitive sports, PE lessons, fitness activities or a range of other outdoor activities.
We aim to provide a PE curriculum that children from EYFS to Year 6 enjoy and fully participate in but which also allows them to experience a range of activities that help them to develop their health, fitness and wellbeing. We intend to offer a high-quality physical education curriculum that inspires all children to succeed and excel in competitive sport and other physically-demanding activities. It provides opportunities for children to become physically confident in a way which supports their health and fitness. Opportunities to compete in sport and other activities build character and help to embed values such as fairness, teamwork, resilience and respect.
At Rowde we recognise that children come to PE with a range of experiences and abilities and make sure that all children are fully supported within PE whatever their needs medical, physical, SEND or well-being. PE at Rowde is fully inclusive and recognises and supports everyone.
Implementation
Staff teaching PE, which includes Acorn PE staff will plan and teach PE lessons using the Complete PE scheme of work. The Complete PE programme provides fun and simple to follow Schemes of Work and support for Early Years Foundation Stage, Key Stage 1 and Key Stage 2 practitioners that give them the confidence and skills to deliver outstanding PE.
It is fully aligned to the proposed National Curriculum and Ofsted requirements and focuses on the development of agility, balance and coordination, healthy competition and cooperative learning. The foundations of the Schemes are based on Fundamental Movement Skills (FMS) of agility, balance and coordination, inclusive competition and broader essential holistic skills (creative, cognitive, social and personal skills).
Impact:
Rowde pupils should demonstrate confidence in a broad range of PE and Sporting skills, evident in lessons and also (for many) in participation in inter-schools and external events. Success in PE should also be evident in their social and personal skills, resilience and sense of team-work.

pageCache.pageTitle: PSHE and RSHE - Rowde C of E Primary Academy
pageCache.text:
PSHE and RSHE
Intent
At Rowde C of E Primary Academy, the intent of our Personal, Social, Health and Economic (PSHE) Education, including Relationships and Health Education, is to develop confident, resilient and compassionate children who are well prepared for life in modern Britain.
Our curriculum equips children with the knowledge, skills and vocabulary they need to build positive relationships, understand and manage their emotions, make informed decisions, keep themselves safe and look after their physical and mental wellbeing. Through carefully sequenced, age-appropriate learning, children explore rights, responsibilities, diversity and respect, developing the confidence to contribute positively to school and the wider community.
As a Church of England school, our Christian vision of Learn, Grow and Love, together with our values of Respect, Optimism, Wisdom, Determination, Enthusiasm and Love, underpin every aspect of our PSHE curriculum, helping children to flourish both academically and personally.
Implementation
We deliver PSHE through the Jigsaw PSHE 3–11 programme, updated for September 2026 and fully aligned with the 2025 Department for Education Relationships, Sex and Health Education guidance. The curriculum provides a carefully sequenced progression from Reception to Year 6 through six half-termly units that revisit and build knowledge, skills and understanding over time.
Each lesson develops children's emotional literacy alongside their knowledge through discussion, reflection, collaborative learning and mindful practice. Our PSHE curriculum includes the statutory teaching of Relationships Education and Health Education, alongside wider learning about citizenship, economic wellbeing, British Values and personal development.
PSHE is embedded throughout school life. Our collective worship, behaviour curriculum, Forest School, educational visits and enrichment opportunities reinforce the knowledge and values taught within lessons. Children also benefit from specialist workshops and safeguarding experiences, including online safety, NSPCC Speak Out Stay Safe, Bikeability, emergency awareness and water safety.
Impact
By the time children leave Rowde, they have developed the confidence, resilience and emotional literacy needed to thrive in the next stage of their education and beyond.
They are able to build positive relationships, communicate respectfully, manage emotions, make informed choices and recognise how to keep themselves physically and emotionally safe. Children understand the importance of kindness, inclusion and respect for others and know when and how to seek support if they are worried or concerned.
The impact of our curriculum is reflected in children's behaviour, wellbeing, confidence and readiness for life beyond primary school. Through regular assessment, pupil voice and curriculum monitoring, we continually review and refine our provision to ensure every child is supported to Learn, Grow and Love.

pageCache.text:
Religion and Worldviews
Our Religion and Worldviews Curriculum
At Rowde, we believe children should leave primary school with more than knowledge about different religions. They should leave with curiosity, empathy and the confidence to ask life's big questions. Our Religion and Worldviews curriculum helps children understand themselves, appreciate others and flourish in an increasingly diverse world.
Intent
At Rowde Church of England Primary Academy, Religion and Worldviews (Religious Education) is rooted in our Christian vision of Learn, Grow, Love, inspired by Jesus' Parable of the Mustard Seed: "Though it is the smallest of all seeds, yet when it grows, it is the largest of garden plants." (Matthew 13:31–32)
Our Religion and Worldviews curriculum encourages children to develop curiosity, ask thoughtful questions and explore a wide range of religious and non-religious worldviews with confidence and respect. We want every child to develop a secure understanding of Christianity, alongside other major world religions and Humanism, recognising the diversity of beliefs, practices and lived experiences within our local, national and global communities.
Through our curriculum, children develop the knowledge and disciplinary skills to think like theologians, social scientists and philosophers, enabling them to investigate beliefs, explore how worldviews shape people's lives and consider life's big questions with increasing confidence. We encourage pupils to reflect on their own ideas while valuing and respecting the beliefs and perspectives of others.
As a Church of England school, Religion and Worldviews makes a significant contribution to children's spiritual, moral, social and cultural development, helping them grow into compassionate, informed and respectful members of society.
Implementation
Religion and Worldviews is a statutory subject and is taught weekly throughout the school.
We follow the RE Today Primary Curriculum, which fulfils the requirements of the Wiltshire Agreed Syllabus for Religious Education (2025–2030) and reflects the expectations of the Church of England Statement of Entitlement.
Children study Christianity throughout their time at Rowde, alongside Judaism, Islam, Hindu Dharma and Humanism. Learning is organised through engaging enquiry questions that encourage pupils to investigate, discuss, reflect and make connections across religions and worldviews.
To strengthen progression, our curriculum is underpinned by Rowde's own progression frameworks for substantive knowledge, disciplinary knowledge, vocabulary and five enduring concepts. These ensure children revisit and deepen their understanding throughout their learning journey. You find out more about these in the downloadable documents below.
Lessons are engaging, discussion-rich and enquiry-led. Children learn through stories, sacred texts, artefacts, visitors, visits to places of worship, philosophy, collaborative discussion and creative activities. They are encouraged to ask questions, justify their thinking using evidence and appreciate the diversity that exists both between and within religions and worldviews.
Impact
Children leave Rowde with a secure understanding of Christianity and a broad knowledge of other religious and non-religious worldviews. They are able to talk confidently about beliefs, values and practices, recognise similarities and differences between worldviews and understand how beliefs influence the lives of individuals and communities.
Our pupils develop the confidence to ask thoughtful questions, think critically, use subject-specific vocabulary accurately and engage respectfully with viewpoints that may differ from their own. Through Religion and Worldviews, children deepen their understanding of themselves, others and the world around them, making a significant contribution to their spiritual development and preparing them well for life in modern Britain.
Assessment is ongoing throughout every enquiry and includes retrieval practice, discussion, observation and reflection, alongside RE Today summative assessment tasks. Teachers also assess children's understanding of our concept and disciplinary progression frameworks, ensuring pupils make sustained progress in both their knowledge and their ability to think as theologians, social scientists and philosophers. The subject leader monitors teaching, learning and assessment through book looks, pupil voice, learning walks and assessment analysis to ensure the curriculum continues to develop and improve.
